turns.content: Can I take leave next month?
Need more detail: how many days and which dates, when you're submitting, your remaining balance, whether you're in probation, and whether a critical delivery period applies.
5 days, Monday 16 to Friday 20 November 2026. I'm submitting the request today, and I've passed probation.

You have 24 working days’ notice, so you meet the 10-working-day minimum for 5 days of leave. Your line manager must approve it after checking your balance, team coverage and any critical delivery period, so approval isn’t guaranteed. Since you’ve passed probation, you may book your full annual entitlement in advance.

conversationalTestCases.scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing how many days, which dates, when the request is submitted, and probation, is asked for it, and replies.
conversationalTestCases.expectedOutcome: Yes, you have given enough notice. Leave of more than 1 and up to 5 working days needs 10 working days' notice, approved by your line manager. Submitting on Tuesday 13 October for leave starting Monday 16 November gives 23 working days' notice, counting neither the submission date nor the first day of leave. The leave still has to be approved in PeopleHub before you take it, and if your team publishes a critical delivery period covering those dates, Head of Department approval is also needed.

turns.content: Will the company pay me while I'm off?
Depends on the type of absence (sickness, family leave, other leave), length of service/probation and eligibility; ask which.
It's sickness. I've worked here for 3 years and passed probation long ago.

With 3 years’ service and probation completed, you can receive 8 weeks at full pay, then 8 weeks at half pay in any rolling 12-month period, if your contract includes the company sick pay scheme. This includes SSP; company sick pay already received in that period is deducted, and reporting or evidence requirements apply.

conversationalTestCases.scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing the type of absence and length of service, is asked for it, and replies.
conversationalTestCases.expectedOutcome: Yes. With 2 years' or more but less than 5 years' continuous service, company sick pay is 8 weeks at full pay, then 8 weeks at half pay, in any rolling 12-month period. Sick pay already paid in the previous 12 months is deducted from that entitlement. It includes Statutory Sick Pay rather than being paid on top of it, and it depends on following the sickness reporting procedure and providing the required evidence.

turns.content: Can I work from home permanently?
Need role designation, whether you mean remote contract, and location (UK only); options are statutory flexible request or contractual change.
I'm in a hybrid role, and I'd work from my home in Manchester.

Possibly, but it needs approval: permanent home working would change your contractual workplace to a remote contract. Request it through a statutory flexible-working application or as part of a role change; the Head of Department and People Operations must approve it. Manchester meets the UK-location requirement.

conversationalTestCases.scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing the role designation and where the employee would work from, is asked for it, and replies.
conversationalTestCases.expectedOutcome: You can ask to become remote-contracted. Changing your contractual place of work to your home is made as a statutory flexible-working request (or as part of a role change), and it needs approval from your Head of Department and People Operations. Your home is in the UK, so it is eligible. Request it normally at least 2 months before the change; if approved, it is recorded in a contract variation letter, and your salary doesn't change.

turns.content: Am I eligible for parental leave?
Which leave: unpaid parental leave, shared parental, paternity, maternity/adoption? Also employee status and parental responsibility/child's age.
I mean unpaid parental leave. I'm an employee, and my daughter is 4.

Yes, if you have parental responsibility for your daughter; employees are eligible from day one for unpaid parental leave for a child under 18. Being named on her birth certificate is one way to qualify.

conversationalTestCases.expectedOutcome: Yes. Unpaid parental leave has been a day-one right since 6 April 2026. With parental responsibility, you can take up to 18 weeks for your daughter before her 18th birthday, at most 4 weeks in any year, in whole weeks, giving 21 days' notice of the start and end dates. Northstar can postpone it by up to 6 months if the business would be unduly disrupted.

turns.content: Can I take my work laptop abroad?
Need purpose (business trip, Work From Abroad, or holiday), destination and data you'll access.
It's a holiday in Spain, and I'd like to work for 3 days while I'm there. I've passed probation.

You can work from Spain for 3 days only with prior approval. Submit a PeopleHub Work From Abroad request at least 4 weeks before; your line manager, People Operations and IT Security must approve it, and Spain must not be on the restricted-destination list. You must also not be serving notice.

The 3 days count toward the 10-working-day rolling 12-month limit. You must be available during UK core hours (10:00–16:00); Restricted information requires written CISO approval and customer-contract permission. Working on holiday abroad without approval breaches the policy.

conversationalTestCases.scenario: The Employee asks a question HR Assist can't answer without knowing the purpose of the trip and the destination, is asked for it, and replies.
conversationalTestCases.expectedOutcome: Working while abroad needs an approved Work From Abroad request. Submit it in PeopleHub at least 4 weeks before you travel; it needs approval from your line manager, People Operations and IT Security. The 3 days count towards the limit of 10 working days in any rolling 12 months. You must be available for UK core hours (10:00 to 16:00 UK time), and you must not access Restricted information without written CISO approval.
